summary: GE-Proton's Wine through rach2-game --umu, umu-launcher and the Steam Linux Runtime's container under Xwayland on virgl: the runtime unpacked once with its updates off, the direct route's Proton settings, Linux's pixels and no refused call in pressure-vessel's log

cases.behavior: rach2-game --umu unpacks the root's Steam Linux Runtime once and runs the 64-bit Direct3D 9 probe through umu-launcher in pressure-vessel's container: the probe reads back Linux's pixels, Proton's log in the container has the direct route's options, fsync and OpenGL renderer, the second start fetches and unpacks nothing, and pressure-vessel's log holds no refused call

execution.privileges: the runner runs as the desktop account, an ordinary user in the render group
execution.cleanup: the runner ends its Wine server and Weston, reaps them and removes its private prefixes, runtime copy, caches and logs on every exit; libetude-case stops QEMU and removes passed overlays, keeping failed overlays and the runner's logs

steps.does: boot an overlay of the GNU system's disk on AHCI with rach2.root=ext2 and the virgl display, log in as root and open the guest command channel
mount the probes' disk read-only and run the umu row as the desktop account through the guest channel, under a headless Weston of its own on GL with Xwayland

assertions.checks: the runtime is unpacked on the first start alone, the probe exits 0 through umu and directly, its CRC-32 equals the stored Linux value, both Proton logs list the same options with wow64 and wined3d, fsync and the OpenGL renderer, pressure-vessel's log has no refused call, and the runner prints GAMESROW OK umu

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the row needs QEMU's virgl display and the Steam Linux Runtime's container, and compares with the Debian guest in the same QEMU
